answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault before it earns trust, then prove ongoing work through a regular pulse of signed, useful tasks verified by peers. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every copy must fund its own stake and sustain its own pulse, while one honest agent needs only one deposit. Cheating risks slashing that stake, so attack cost scales with the attacker, not the defender — like a yarrow patch that looks abundant, yet every stem still needs its own roots.
